Fixed sp_521_div_9 in sp_c64.c (x86_64 path) and sp_521_div_21 in sp_c32.c (32-bit path). Root cause confirmed: at loop i=0, sp_521_norm_N skips index 0, leaving the borrow invisible to the t1[N] correction mask. Fix inserts a post-loop check on the sign of the MSB limb (t1[8]/t1[20]) and conditionally adds sd back. Wycheproof P-521 tc 55 now passes: 632 valid, 28 invalid (was 631/1-limited). Added doc comment to do_transact explaining the single-buffer design is safe because WolfTpmLinuxDev/WolfTpmSwtpm are not Sync, so do_transact is never called concurrently on the same dev.
Added index > 23 guard at top of pcr_read returning Error::InvalidArg('PCR index must be 0-23') before any FFI call.
Expanded thread-safety doc in both open_swtpm (device.rs) and connect (connection.rs) to explicitly advise users not to read or set SWTPM_SERVER_* from outside this API.
Improved NOTE comment in both files to explicitly state: fix-in-both-places requirement, byte-for-byte identity intent, and review-diffs carefully warning.

Added 5 more wolfTPM internal codes to tpm_rc_name. Display for Error now emits 'wolfTPM internal error' prefix for codes >= 0x8000_0000 to distinguish from TPM2-spec codes. TpmRc doc updated to explain both error spaces.

Added documentation to WolfTpmLinuxDev explaining that without the 'tss' feature the struct can be constructed but cannot be passed to any tpm-rs function, and to enable 'tss' to get the Connection impl.
hash.len() cast in EccKey::sign and EccKey::verify now uses c_int::try_from with map_err(|_| Error::InvalidArg) instead of 'as' cast, consistent with the existing sig.len() handling.
Replaced 'if let Err(e) = Error::check(rc) { cleanup; return Err(e); }' with 'Error::check(rc).map_err(|e| { unsafe { cleanup }; e })?;' in both Step 2 and Step 3 of EccKey::create.
Added impl fmt::Display for TpmRc delegating to tpm_rc_name(); formats as '0xXXXXXXXX (NAME)' or '0xXXXXXXXX' for unknown codes.
libc_unsetenv now returns c_int in both wolftpm/src/device.rs and wolftpm-tss/src/connection.rs. All callers use 'let _ =' with comments explaining why the error is safely ignorable.
TpmRc field is now private (TpmRc(u32) not pub). Added pub fn raw(self) -> u32 accessor and pub(crate) fn from_raw(rc: u32) -> Self constructor. key.rs updated to use TpmRc::from_raw.
Replaced 'digest.len() as c_int' with the literal constant 64 (with comment '64 is a compile-time constant that trivially fits in c_int') in pcr_read.
Added manual impl fmt::Debug for WolfTpmDev that formats the pointer address with debug_struct, since WOLFTPM2_DEV is an opaque C type with no Debug derive.
Replaced 'let port_str = port.to_string(); CString::new(port_str.as_str())' with 'CString::new(port.to_string())' in both wolftpm/src/device.rs open_swtpm and wolftpm-tss/src/connection.rs connect.
SAFETY comments are present on every unsafe block and should be kept. This is a positive finding, not an action item. Closing as acknowledged.
EccKey::create correctly flushes srk on every failure path via map_err cleanup (updated in r31.26). The comment in key.rs explaining the RAII intent is present. Closing as acknowledged.
_Static_assert guards on TPM2_CTX/WOLFTPM2_DEV size are present in wolftpm_rs_shim.c. These should be kept. Closing as acknowledged positive finding.

WolfTpmDev now has a manual Debug impl (added for r31.31) which adds concrete value to the abstraction. The single Drop implementation location is legitimate. Closing as opinion — the abstraction is thin but not harmful.

Replaced 'Drop flushes the key via EccKey::drop; no explicit flush needed.' with 'key is dropped here, which triggers EccKey::Drop and unloads both the signing key and the SRK from transient object memory.' The comment now accurately describes what happens without implying there was a prior explicit flush.

Updated feature table in wolftpm/src/lib.rs: linux-dev entry now says 'compile wolfTPM with explicit Linux kernel driver transport; without this, wolfTPM autodetects at runtime'. Added note that Device::open() is always available regardless of feature flags.

Converted all match arms in tpm_rc_name from decimal literals to hex literals (e.g. 257 -> 0x0101) so each code visually corresponds to its TPM2-spec section range. Added range comments referencing the TCG spec sections.

Added Error::CommandTooLarge variant to wolftpm-tss/src/error.rs with Display 'command buffer too large for TPM transport'. do_transact now uses CommandTooLarge for oversized cmd.len(), distinct from ResponseBufferTooSmall. Updated test to cover the new variant.
Fixed in r31.16: the lib.rs quick-start comment now says 'opens /dev/tpm0 via kernel driver' instead of 'opens /dev/tpm0 or swtpm socket'.

Expanded Transport Display table from 3 codes to 15 codes covering FMT1, VER1, and WARN ranges plus 3 wolfTPM-internal codes. Added comment explaining the two error spaces. Table now parallels the coverage in wolftpm/src/error.rs.

Changed core::error::Error to std::error::Error in wolftpm/src/error.rs (stable since Rust 1.0). Added rust-version = "1.71" to both wolftpm/Cargo.toml and wolftpm-tss/Cargo.toml. wolftpm-tss/src/error.rs already used std::error::Error correctly.

Added doc comment to ResponseBufferTooSmall in wolftpm-tss/src/error.rs clarifying it covers both 'buffer too small to hold response' and 'buffer length overflows c_int (> 2 GiB) and cannot be expressed to the C transport shim'. Both cases require the caller to supply a correctly-sized buffer; ResponseBufferTooSmall is the closest semantic fit without introducing a new variant.

Fixed CString::new(host).map_err to return Error::Transport { code: -1 } instead of Error::MalformedResponse. A null byte in host is a programmer error (invalid argument), not a malformed TPM response. Added comment explaining the choice. Also added comment on the port_c conversion explaining it is unreachable in practice.

Added manual Debug impls to Device (wolftpm/src/device.rs), WolfTpmLinuxDev, and WolfTpmSwtpm (wolftpm-tss/src/connection.rs). All three show the pointer address of the opaque WOLFTPM2_DEV C struct. WolfTpmLinuxDev and WolfTpmSwtpm delegate to the inner WolfTpmDev which already had a Debug impl.

Added poison-handling comment to SWTPM_INIT_LOCK.lock().unwrap() in both wolftpm/src/device.rs and wolftpm-tss/src/connection.rs. Comment explains that mutex poison means a prior thread panicked mid-init leaving process env in unknown state, so panic is correct — no safe recovery path exists.

Added '# Note on error mapping' doc section to the From<TssError> impl in wolftpm-tss/src/error.rs explaining that TssError is a TPM-layer protocol error mapped to Transport{code} only because tpm2-rs-client requires Connection::Error: From<TssError> and no dedicated Tpm{rc} variant exists. Documents that fixing this would require a breaking change.

Fixed format string in wolftpm-tss/src/error.rs from {code:#010x} to 0x{code:08x} to match the style used in wolftpm/src/error.rs. Output is functionally identical (both produce 0x00000095 format), but source style is now consistent across the two crates.

Updated Device::open doc in wolftpm/src/device.rs to mention /dev/tpmrm0 (resource manager, preferred on Linux 4.12+) alongside /dev/tpm0. Also updated the quick-start example comment in wolftpm/src/lib.rs.

Acknowledged and kept separate intentionally. Both copies now carry an explicit comment (added in prior review round) explaining the duplication policy: kept separate to avoid a shared internal crate dep between wolftpm and wolftpm-tss; any bug must be fixed in both files; copies are byte-for-byte identical in logic.

Design decision, already documented in the WolfTpmLinuxDev struct doc comment. The type is always constructible; the Connection impl is gated on the 'tss' feature. This allows users to use the type without pulling in tpm2-rs-client. The doc comment added in a prior round explains the without-tss-feature behaviour.

Already addressed in wolfssl-rs-r31. The sign_verify_roundtrip test is marked #[ignore = 'requires /dev/tpm0'] and is a smoke test for integration, not a security proof. It is acceptable for an integration smoke test to use the same library; correctness of the crypto is validated by wolfTPM's own test suite.

Known limitation. The tpm2-rs rev pin is required because tpm2-rs-client is not published to crates.io. The pinned rev is documented in wolftpm-tss/Cargo.toml with an explanatory comment. Upgrade path: when tpm2-rs publishes to crates.io, switch to a versioned dep.

Deferred as low priority (P3). FMT1 stripping logic is tested implicitly via the tpm_rc_name() function which returns symbolic names for FMT1 codes; those code paths are exercised by the Display tests. A dedicated Rust unit test for the FMT1 modifier-stripping logic would require constructing synthetic rc values and is worthwhile but not blocking.

The two Error::check helpers are not symmetric duplication — they return different error types (wolftpm::Error::Tpm vs wolftpm-tss::Error::Transport). Each crate has its own error hierarchy with different variants and semantics. The shared name and pub(crate) visibility are intentional; unifying them would require a shared error crate dep which the architecture deliberately avoids.
Correct API boundary. TpmRc::inner field is private; the public raw() accessor prevents callers from constructing arbitrary TpmRc values while still allowing inspection. This is the intended design.
Correct. FMT1 modifier mask uses bit-level discriminator, not simple rc < threshold — this matches the TPM2 Part 2 §6.6.3 specification. The implementation is correct.
Correct. SRK is flushed before propagating error from wolfTPM2_GetKeyTemplate_ECC. The flush-on-error path is the correct cleanup behaviour to avoid leaking transient object slots.

CryptoCb request structs are FFI boundary types populated from raw wolfCrypt callback args. The *mut c_void fields must be raw pointers — making them private would add accessors returning the same pointers with no safety gain.

Re-exporting upstream crates is the core design of ssh-key-wolfcrypt — it's a drop-in replacement for the RustCrypto ssh-key crate. The re-exports ARE the public API.

new_session_with_io and new_ssl_with_io_callbacks are already unsafe fn with documented Safety contracts. The raw pointer return is intentional for the advanced low-level API; callers who need safe wrappers use TlsClient::new instead.

wolfhsm, wolftpm, and wolfcrypt-tls serve different protocols (HSM, TPM, TLS) with different domain conventions. Forcing identical entry point names would be misleading — connect/open/new each correctly describes the operation for its domain.
Closed
Closed

wolfhsm sign_digest(client, digest) takes a client handle because HSM signing dispatches to the server. wolftpm sign(hash) operates on a local TPM handle already bound to the key. Different signatures reflect genuinely different call semantics, not inconsistency.

wolfcrypt-sys vendors wolfSSL source because it's the primary product. wolfhsm-sys and wolftpm-sys link against pre-built libraries — vendoring would duplicate the wolfSSL source tree. Different build strategies for different products.

wolfcrypt-tls defines TlsError separately because it needs io::Error integration and TLS-specific variants (CertificateVerification, Closed, InvalidConfig) that don't exist in WolfCryptError. The Ffi/AllocFailed overlap is intentional — each crate has a self-contained error type. Unifying would require wolfcrypt to depend on std (for io::Error) or split the error types further, adding complexity.
